title: Implied requirements - nothing stated as a requirement
purpose: The posting never lists a tool, a library or a qualification. Everything a reader would infer is left as a description of the work. It exists to see whether the assistant invents a requirement list when the text supplies none, and whether it stays quiet on fields the posting gives it no purchase on.
text:
Product Analyst Intern
Northwind Analytics, Singapore

We are a small team and we write everything down. The intern we are looking for
will spend the first month shadowing the analysts, then take over the weekly
numbers that go to the leadership meeting.

You do not need to arrive knowing our stack. You do need to be the kind of
person who, when a number looks wrong, keeps pulling the thread until they can
explain why it looked wrong.

Day to day you will
- keep the weekly numbers honest and explain the movements in a short note
- sit with the sales team and write down what they actually ask for
- turn those asks into something the engineers can pick up

The numbers live in a warehouse you will query directly, and the notes are
written in a plain text editor. We care more about how you think than about a
list of tools on your resume.
notes: No canonical skill token appears anywhere in the text, so skill_overlap() returns 0.0 by construction (an empty requirement set scores 0.0, not 1.0). The measured retrieval score sits 0.024 under the abstention threshold, which is the most interesting number in this file: a posting a human would call clearly relevant lands on the declining side of the line. Any requirement list the assistant reports for this posting was inferred, not extracted.
